title: Vasquez and Valentia call it simply conditional, reducible to the other two; a dispute about words
source_text: XI. Nihilominus scientiam istam futurorum sub conditione nonnulli, non mediam, sed conditionatam simpliciter appellant, quoniam censent illam facile revocari posse, vel ad scientiam visionis, juxta quosdam; vel juxta plures alios, ad scientiam simplicis intelligentiae: quo de numero sunt Vasquez & Gregorius de Valentia. Quanquam observat Vasquez nihil obesse, si doctrinae & claritatis gratia, inter duas illas scientiae divinae species tertium aliquod membrum constituatur: atque hanc dissensionem vocum esse, non rerum, nec multum referre, si qui hac in re varie loquantur. Tom. 1. disp. 67. sub finem.
pass_a_gloss: XI. Nevertheless some call that knowledge of futures under a condition, not middle, but simply conditional, because they judge that it can easily be brought back, either to the knowledge of vision, according to some; or according to many others, to the knowledge of simple intelligence: of which number are Vasquez and Gregory of Valentia. Although Vasquez observes that nothing stands in the way, if for the sake of teaching and clarity, some third member be constituted between those two species of divine knowledge: and that this is a dissension of words, not of things, nor does it matter much, if some speak variously in this matter. Vol. 1, disp. 67, towards the end.
pass_b_english: Some, however, call this knowledge of future things under a condition not 'middle' but simply 'conditional'. They think it can easily be reduced either to the knowledge of vision, as some hold, or, as many more hold, to the knowledge of simple intelligence. Vasquez and Gregory of Valentia are among these.

Vasquez does note, though, that nothing prevents setting up some third category between those two kinds of divine knowledge for the sake of teaching and clarity. The disagreement, he says, is about words, not things, and it matters little if people speak differently on the point. Volume 1, disputation 67, near the end.

choices.why: Knowledge of what would happen under a condition; kept as the technical counterpart to middle knowledge.
